This module cites no AICPA text — SOC 2's structure (Type I/Type II, the five Trust Services
Criteria, CUECs, bridge letters) is named and described only, the same handling this curriculum
gives every paid, proprietary framework (ISO 31000, ISO 19011, GAMP 5). The links below are
AICPA's own public overview pages about the SOC 2 suite, a video, several professional reading
guides, plus the internal-course link back to module 1. All were checked with `curl` and returned a live page at the time this page was written;
AICPA's site is a JavaScript-rendered application, so these links are verified as reachable, live
AICPA pages about SOC 2 — not as a source of quotable text, which this curriculum has never
fetched or read.

- **[AICPA & CIMA: SOC 2](https://www.aicpa-cima.com/resources/landing/soc-2)** — AICPA's own
  public landing page for the SOC 2 service. Use it as the starting point for understanding what
  SOC 2 is and who produces it (an accounting profession, not a healthcare or blood-industry
  regulator) — not as a source for exact Trust Services Criteria wording, which sits behind the
  paid guidance this curriculum has never purchased.

- **[AICPA & CIMA: SOC for Service Organizations](https://www.aicpa-cima.com/topic/audit-assurance/audit-and-assurance-greater-than-soc-2-greater-than-soc-for-service-organizations)**
  — AICPA's own topic page situating SOC 2 inside the broader SOC (System and Organization
  Controls) family of reports. Useful for seeing, from the source body itself, that SOC 2 is one
  report type among several AICPA offers, each scoped to a different audience and purpose.

- **[Supplier Qualification and Risk Tiering](../supplier-qualification-and-risk-tiering/index.qmd)**
  — module 1 of this course, where the device-management platform vendor was locked into the
  High tier this module's whole exercise assumes, using the four-question scheme (data touch,
  system criticality, access level, blast radius) this module builds directly on. Read it first
  if you haven't, or re-read it to recall exactly why this vendor earned the scrutiny a SOC 2
  report review represents.

- **[AICPA & CIMA: System and Organization Controls (SOC) suite of services](https://www.aicpa-cima.com/resources/landing/system-and-organization-controls-soc-suite-of-services)**
  — AICPA's own overview of the full SOC family (SOC 1, 2, 3 and others), useful for telling
  which report a vendor actually handed you. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[How To Read SOC 2 TYPE 2. Vendor Assessment. SOC Reports. WorkLifeCyber](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GsMxisYYShA)**
  (Worklifecyber, from oEmbed `author_name`) — the video embedded in this lesson: a practitioner
  walkthrough of reading a Type II report during a vendor assessment. Industry training content,
  not AICPA guidance, and not blood-industry-specific. Verified embeddable via YouTube oEmbed on
  2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[SANS Institute: An Expert's Guide to Reviewing SOC 2 Reports](https://www.sans.org/blog/expert-guide-reviewing-soc2-reports)**
  — a well-known security-training organization's guide to what to look for when reading a vendor's
  report. Read it for a second opinion on scope, exceptions, and the customer-side controls.
  Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[Compass IT Compliance: How to Read a SOC 2 Report, a Section-by-Section Guide](https://www.compassitc.com/blog/how-to-read-a-soc-2-report-a-section-by-section-guide)**
  — an audit-firm walkthrough covering the auditor's opinion, system description, controls testing,
  and CUECs in report order. Useful for the parts of a report this lesson names but doesn't
  tour, such as how the auditor's opinion and listed exceptions relate. Verified loading via
  `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[Fractional CISO: How to Read A SOC 2 Report](https://fractionalciso.com/how-to-read-a-soc-2-report/)**
  — a practitioner explainer on key takeaways when reviewing a report as a customer. Vendor-published
  commentary, so use it as a cross-check, not an authority. Verified loading via `curl` on
  2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

## Keep learning

Not official sources — good places to learn more about reading SOC reports and third-party assurance.

- **[Subservice Organization Management — IT Controls for Peace of Mind](https://www.isaca.org/resources/isaca-journal/issues/2023/volume-4/subservice-organization-management-it-controls-for-peace-of-mind)** (ISACA Journal, 2023) — explains how a vendor's own vendors show up in SOC reports and what to do about them; pairs well with the scope and carve-out questions in this lesson. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[Third-Party Risk Management: SOC Reporting](https://hbkcpa.com/insights/third-party-risk-management-soc-reporting/)** (HBK, CPA firm) — a practitioner's explanation of the report types and what a reader should look for; written by an audit firm, so a view from the preparer's side of the table. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[Leveraging SOC Reports for Effective Third-Party Risk Management](https://www.forvismazars.us/forsights/2025/06/leveraging-soc-reports-for-effective-third-party-risk-management)** (Forvis Mazars US, CPA firm) — how to turn a SOC report into follow-up questions and monitoring rather than a filed PDF. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[The Assurance Gap: Five Questions to Ask Before Relying on an Assurance Report](https://hitrustalliance.net/blog/the-assurance-gap-five-questions-to-ask-before-relying-on-an-assurance-report)** (HITRUST — an assurance-framework vendor, so read with that in mind) — a skeptical checklist for what a report does and doesn't tell you. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[CCT 364: Third Party Risk Management - How One Vendor Breach Exposed 119,000 Users](https://cisspcybertrainingpodcast.buzzsprout.com/2167626/episodes/19586550-cct-364-third-party-risk-management-how-one-vendor-breach-exposed-119-000-users)** (CISSP Cyber Training Podcast) — a CISSP-prep episode on a vendor breach and third-party risk; supports CISSP Domain 1 (and Domain 6 on assessment and audit strategy). Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
